tasks.summary: provenance.ts implements resolveDesignCoverage and validateDesignRetainedSource largely matching the two acceptance checks (strictly-backward resolution, cycle/forward/foreign/missing/invalidated/malformed rejection, immutability of history, bypass guard). However the "root" check that pins every hop's report to the same review uses `history[0]?.report` instead of any attempt in history that actually carries a report. When the earliest trusted attempt has no report (e.g. it was invalidated or interrupted before completing — a state the design's own recovery/invalidation model explicitly allows), `root` is `undefined` and every otherwise-valid resolution is wrongly rejected with `invalid_checkpoint`. This was later corrected (outside this task's scope, commit 76d3d899a) to `history.find(a=>a.report)?.report`, confirming the defect was real. Test coverage is otherwise thorough (an 11-mutation rejection matrix plus a positive-chain test with reference-identity assertions), but it never exercises either (a) a first-attempt-without-report history, or (b) the distinct mismatch-rejection branch unique to `validateDesignRetainedSource` (every test either hits resolveDesignCoverage's own incomplete-check first or exercises the matching, non-bypass case), so the acceptance item "reject older-passed bypass of immediately preceding incomplete coverage" is not actually proven for the comparison guard itself.

findings.message: `const root=history[0]?.report;` assumes the earliest attempt in the trusted history slice always has a completed report. When history[0] lacks a report (e.g. an invalidated or interrupted first attempt, which the design's recovery/invalidation states explicitly allow), `root` is undefined, so `requireDesign(root && ...)` fails and resolveDesignCoverage incorrectly rejects every otherwise-valid backward reference in that history with 'invalid_checkpoint', even when a later attempt holds the real originating report. The correct fix (`history.find(a=>a.report)?.report`) was applied in a later, out-of-scope commit (76d3d899a), confirming this is a genuine defect in the code submitted for this task.
findings.rationale: Breaks the task's primary acceptance check ('resolve strictly decreasing same-artifact/reviewer references to accepted substantive sources') under a state the design itself anticipates (subject-only invalidation / explicit restarts per LLD citation c2), causing valid provenance chains to fail closed instead of resolving.

findings.message: No test exercises a history whose earliest attempt lacks a `.report` (the exact precondition for the root-fallback defect above), and no test exercises the mismatch path unique to `validateDesignRetainedSource`'s own guard (`baseline.attempt===candidate.attempt && baseline.chunk.id===candidate.chunk.id`). The one test labelled to cover 'older-passed bypass of immediately preceding incomplete coverage' (the `newer` fixture) actually fails earlier inside `resolveDesignCoverage`'s own incomplete-result check while resolving the baseline itself, so `validateDesignRetainedSource`'s distinguishing comparison line is never actually driven to reject a mismatched-but-individually-valid baseline/candidate pair.
findings.rationale: Acceptance check 2 explicitly requires rejecting an older-passed bypass of the immediately preceding coverage; the implementation's distinct guard for this is present but unverified by any test, and the coverage gap directly correlates with the undetected production defect above.

testCoverage.explanation: Inspected both test bodies against the acceptance checks: the positive test asserts strictly-backward resolution and reference-identity preservation of historical findings (no copying); the matrix test runs 11 targeted mutations (self/forward-pointing retained reference, wrong reviewer, foreign artifactId/reviewId, invalidated source, missing/duplicated/both-fresh-and-retained origin, incomplete source, limitations present, absent chunk id) plus malformed-stored-result, non-contiguous-history, missing-reviewer, and no-mutation immutability checks. This is a thorough, evidence-backed completion of the coverage review (not an execution claim). The review surfaced two concrete gaps, reported as findings above, rather than leaving the coverage assessment itself incomplete.

tasks.summary: The impact-attempt consolidation/reconciliation logic (results.ts, checkpoint.ts, coordinator.ts, policy.ts) correctly implements the exact F=S/S⊔R=P partition, final-result-only finding reconciliation, retained-only-carry protection, and dedup-by-immutable-tuple semantics, all backed by the four new fixture-driven tests which pass. However, consolidateImpactReview's self-consistency re-derivation of each fresh chunk result (results.ts:135) drops the requiredReferences (live document path, and checkpoint path for the final chunk) that the real review flow enforces (coordinator.ts:285), creating an asymmetry that lets a forged/corrupted completedChunks entry skip the document-citation requirement while still passing checkIdentity's invalid_checkpoint re-validation.

findings.message: consolidateImpactReview's re-derivation of each fresh chunk result calls assessDesignResult(results[i], selected[i]!, results.slice(0,i), [], {...}) with an empty requiredReferences array, whereas the live review flow (coordinator.ts:285) calls the same function with requiredReferences = [checkpoint.subject.documentPath, ...(chunk.purpose==='consistency' ? [path] : [])]. Because assessDesignResult's requiredReferences default is also '[]' (results.ts:79), this re-derivation silently drops the requirement that every fresh chunk cite the live document path (and the final consistency chunk also cite the checkpoint path) in inspectedReferences or limitations. checkIdentity (checkpoint.ts:127) uses this same re-derivation as its integrity gate for accepting an impact attempt's stored report; a completedChunks entry that was hand-constructed (e.g. a forged/corrupted checkpoint written directly via saveDesignCheckpoint, bypassing the coordinator) with status 'passed' and no documentPath citation anywhere will reproduce byte-identically under the weakened re-check and therefore pass validation, even though the real validate path would have forced that same chunk to 'incomplete' for missing required coverage.
findings.rationale: This is a genuine asymmetry introduced by this task's new consolidateImpactReview code: the function that is supposed to prove 'this stored attempt is exactly what a correct review pass would produce' (per its own purpose, used by checkIdentity to reject tampered checkpoints) omits one of the two required-reference checks that the production path applies to every chunk. It weakens the acceptance guarantee of 'fresh-only result bodies ... complete inventory coverage' specifically for the document/checkpoint-path citation requirement during impact attempts.
